entries.label: Room tileset sample (wall with doorway + floor panels)
entries.notes: 160x128 composite structural sample, not a placeable prop. Upper half y64-127 is the wall layer (64px = 4 tiles tall; y64 is a 1px dark base line). x0-7 and x56-63 are 8px wall-end/door-jamb pillars with a darker top cap (y124-127) flanking a fully transparent 48px opening (x8-55, y64-127, a 3-tile doorway gap). x64-159 is a grey-blue back-wall face topped by an orange band. On the left (x64-101) the band is y125-127 above a red line at y124. The red edge then steps diagonally down from x102 (y123) to x122 (y117) and continues as a red line at y116 from x123 to x159, so on the right the orange band deepens to y117-127. A pale glow band at the bottom of the wall face covers y65-67 at full width and rises in matching steps (x102-122) to y75 on the right (x123-159). Lower half y0-63 is the floor layer: six 32x32 riveted metal floor panels (x0-95) and plain speckled floor (x96-159). Slice into 16px tiles or 9-slice before use.

entries.label: Tiny blue wall status panel
entries.notes: 7x8 framed mini screen with a cyan glyph (a bar over two dots), in the same palette as the blue screens 3 and 12. Blue variant of 10. Reads as a door access panel, light switch or status LED. Small enough to also work as a desk gadget or floor marker; the current level appears to scatter it on the floor.

entries.label: Orange wall terminal screen (portrait)
entries.notes: 20x26 flat, front-facing framed panel: an orange text screen (y6-22) over a control strip with one button at x3,y3 and grey slots (y2-4). It has no top face or base, so it reads as wall-mounted (a wall terminal or kiosk). Orange variant of 3; portrait counterpart of 11. If it must stand on the floor, use a footprint of about x1,y0,w18,h4.

entries.label: Blue wall terminal screen (portrait)
entries.notes: Blue/cyan variant of 2 (identical layout). The current level stands this sprite on the floor for the case terminals C-101 to C-701. The art has no base, so it looks best hung on the back-wall face with the interaction zone on the floor tile in front. If kept on the floor, use a footprint of about x1,y0,w18,h4.

entries.label: Wall server/cooling unit with fan and status screen
entries.notes: 57x25 box: a large round fan (x5-22, y2-17), a cyan screen with text lines and a bar graph (x25-46, y3-17), a green LED at x49 and a red LED at x51 (y3-4). The top face is only 4px (y20-23, outline at y24), the same build and palette as 15, which also has a 4px top and which the current level stands on the floor as the ADA station. Floor furniture in this pack has deeper tops (desk 35: 7px, fridge 43: about 15px), so this reads best as a shallow wall-mounted unit (HVAC, server or AI core). A thin floor cabinet against the wall is a weaker alternative reading. Strong AI-core/ADA candidate, used from the floor tile in front. If placed on the floor anyway, use footprint x0,y0,w57,h5.

entries.label: Office/gaming chair, back view
entries.notes: 17x26 swivel chair facing north (back to the camera). The backrest (y9-25) carries a blue 'LIH' logo. A dark seat band sits at y7-8 (x0-16). The 5-star caster base is a diamond at y0-6, x4-12 (widest at y3 and y5; bottom tip x8-9 at y0), and the footprint is exactly that box. Place it just south of a desk or terminal; the tall backrest is drawn over the player when he walks behind it. A solid chair in front of an interactive desk can block access, so keep the trigger reachable or make this chair non-solid there. Unrelated to the armchair set (23/24, 46/47).

entries.label: Light-blue single-pedestal table/bench
entries.notes: 32x19, seen from the front. A light-blue slab: the top surface is y8-18 (face y9-17 with a highlight row at y17, a front lip at y8 and an outline at y18). Below it are a 1px front edge at y7 and a dark underside strip at y6. Three indicator lights sit on its left rim at x2: cyan at y14, blue at y13 and y11. It rests on a single closed dark pedestal at bottom-left (x0-11, y0-5, rounded bottom-left corner); x12-31, y0-5 is transparent overhang. The footprint is the slab projected to the floor across its full width: the top is about 8px above the floor, so the back edge at y18 lands near y10. Exact identity is uncertain: it could be an exam/med table, a low bench or a cot. Alternative reading: a wall-mounted AC unit, where the full-width dark strip at y6 is the air outlet and the pedestal is a bracket. If it is hung on a wall that way, make it non-solid with footprint 0. Can be flipped horizontally.

entries.label: HOME SWEET HOME neon sign
entries.notes: 62x29 flat sign: magenta neon border on navy, pink 'HOME SWEET HOME' text, a cyan house icon and cyan/yellow accent bars at top-right. Decorative only. The current level already hangs it on a wall.

entries.label: Large wall window/screen frame (empty, see-through)
entries.notes: 78x25. A rounded white/grey frame around an orange inner border (x4-73, y3-20) with small HUD marks: signal bars at bottom-right, dashes at top-right and a glyph at bottom-left. The interior is fully transparent, so it shows whatever is behind it (a parallax backdrop or the wall). Empty variant of 9. The HUD marks suggest a smart window or holo-display. 18 and 26 look like further frame variants.

entries.label: Large wall window/screen with night city skyline
entries.notes: Same 78x25 frame and orange HUD border as 8, filled with a purple night skyline (lit windows in orange, yellow, pink and cyan). Decorative. The current level uses this style on a wall. 19 and 27 look like variants.

entries.label: Tiny orange wall status panel
entries.zoneUse: any (next to doors and consoles; alert/locked indicator)
entries.notes: Orange/red variant of 1: the same 7x8 layout in the palette of the orange screens 2 and 11. Works as a door access panel, light switch or alert LED; could also be a desk gadget or floor marker.

entries.label: Small orange wall monitor (landscape)
entries.notes: 18x15 flat framed screen: orange with yellow text lines and blocks. It has no stand and no top face, so it hangs on a wall. Orange variant of 12; landscape counterpart of 2. Display only, though it could double as a secondary wall terminal. 21 and 31 are larger monitors on stands.

entries.label: Small blue wall monitor (landscape)
entries.notes: Blue/cyan variant of 11 (identical layout): 18x15 flat framed screen with cyan text lines. Hangs on a wall. Display only; could double as a secondary wall terminal.

entries.label: Low tech console with open shelf (3 colored canisters)
entries.notes: Pair with 14 (same body, empty shelf). Knee-high unit: dark front y0-7, light top y8-14 with orange LEDs. Open cubby on the front (x2-24, y2-6) holds red/blue/green capped canisters (x2-10). Rounded cyan end cap with a blue light on the right (x25-28); the left end is flat, so it can butt against a left wall or be mirrored. Faces down/south. Could also be read as a battery rack or media console.

entries.label: Low tech console with empty open shelf
entries.notes: Empty-shelf variant of 13, otherwise identical. The cubby recess runs x2-24, y2-6. Flat left end, rounded cyan cap on the right. Faces down/south.

entries.label: Wall data terminal panel
entries.notes: Shallow wall box: a 4-px light top band (y17-20, outline at y21) over a 16-px front (y1-16). Six horizontal lines on the left (x2-18, y4-14) read as a text list or as vent slats. Blue status screen on the right (x20-27, y4-12). Cyan LED (x2-4) and two dark buttons (x20-21, x23-24) at y2. Faces down/south. The body palette (117,149,177 front / 173,201,225 top) and the top-band build match wall unit 4 (the fan/AC box), not screens 2/3/11/12, which supports reading it as a wall piece. Could also pass for a climate-control unit. If stood on the floor against a wall instead, use a footprint of about x1,y0,w28,h5. The old level (current_level.png) used it as the ADA station.

entries.label: Counter-top sink with faucet and drainboard
entries.notes: Pair with 17 (water-filled). Basin seen from above (x6-27, y0-10). Faucet with blue/red hot-cold knobs sits at the back and pokes above the rim (x14-19, y6-12). Slatted drainboard on the left (x0-4, odd rows). It has no cabinet front, so it is an overlay for a counter top. It is 28x13, which fits the 30x13 light counter tops in slice 25 (sub-rects 32,0 / 64,0 / 32,35 / 64,35).

entries.label: Counter-top sink filled with water
entries.notes: Water-filled variant of 16: light-blue water fills the basin, with the drain visible underneath. Use it the same way, as an overlay on a counter top (fits the slice 25 counter tops).

entries.label: Panoramic window frame, pink neon trim (empty)
entries.zoneUse: lounge, office, any room on an exterior wall
entries.notes: Frame-only variant of 19. The interior is transparent, so put a backdrop or parallax layer behind it, or use it as an empty/dark screen frame. Size 78x25 (about 4.9x1.6 tiles). Pale rounded frame with a thin pink inner neon line and pink HUD marks in three corners. Same family: 8/9 (orange trim) and 26/27 (cyan trim). Goes on the back wall face.

entries.label: Panoramic window, night city skyline, pink trim
entries.zoneUse: lounge, office, bedroom, any room on an exterior wall
entries.notes: Filled variant of 18: purple night skyline with lit windows and neon signs, plus the same pink HUD marks. Twins: 9 (orange trim) and 27 (cyan trim). Reads as an exterior window or a large city-feed display. Size 78x25, for the back wall face.

entries.label: Angled side monitor, cyan (left wing of 21)
entries.zoneUse: office, security, server room, command center
entries.notes: Left wing of a triple-monitor desk rig. The sheet draws it together with center screen 21, keyboard 28 and mouse 29. Its offset from 21's bottom-left corner is (-16,-8): a 2-px gap, with its bottom 8 px lower than 21's. That puts its inner right edge (y11-27) exactly level with 21's screen frame (y3-19). Its edges are 17 px tall and slant up toward 21, so the outer end is nearer the viewer. The thick frame is on the outer left side. It has no stand, so it sits on the same desk or counter top as 21. Mirror is 22; the orange version is 30. It is not a back-wall piece. It would only fit a side wall drawn slanted, and this game's side walls are not slanted.

entries.label: Holo monitor on stand, cyan (front-facing)
entries.zoneUse: office, security, command center, investigation desk
entries.notes: Front-facing cyan holo monitor: screen frame y3-19 on a small stand base (x13-18, y0-2). Place it on a desk or counter top. The screen shows text lines plus a photo box, like a personnel or ID file, which suits an investigation case. The sheet draws it as the center of a workstation set. Offsets from 21's bottom-left corner: left wing 20 at (-16,-8), right wing 22 at (+34,-8), keyboard 28 at (+9,-8), mouse 29 at (+27,-7). The full rig is 64x28 px, as wide as two slice-25 counter modules, and the assembled rig would also make a good ada_console station. The orange set is 31 with wings 30/32, keyboard 37 and mouse 38, at the same offsets.

entries.label: Angled side monitor, cyan (right wing of 21)
entries.zoneUse: office, security, server room, command center
entries.notes: Right wing of the triple-monitor desk rig and the mirror of 20. Its offset from 21's bottom-left corner is (+34,-8): a 2-px gap, with its bottom 8 px lower than 21's. That puts its inner left edge (y11-27) exactly level with 21's screen frame (y3-19). It slants up to the left toward 21, and the thick frame is on the outer right side. It has no stand, so it sits on the same desk or counter top as 21. The orange version is 32. It is not a back-wall piece, because this game's side walls are not drawn slanted.

entries.label: Red pod armchair, front view
entries.notes: Faces down/south. Pair with blue 24. Back views are probably 46 (red) / 47 (blue); side views are 33/34 (facing right) and 40/41. Base y0-3, seat cushion y4-11 (crease at y11), armrests x0-24 up to y15. The rounded backrest (y12-29) draws over anyone walking behind it. The footprint covers base + seat + backrest thickness.

entries.label: Blue pod armchair, front view
entries.notes: Blue twin of 23 and 1 px wider (26x30). Faces down/south. Back view is probably 47; side views are 34 and 41. Same layout as 23: seat y4-11, armrests full width up to y15, backrest y12-29 drawn over anyone behind it.

entries.label: Merged sheet: neon sign, wall panel, 4 counter blocks
entries.zoneUse: mixed: reception, kitchen, shop, office, lounge, AI station (after re-slicing)
entries.notes:
Several touching sprites merged by the slicer; re-slice before use. Rects are (x,y,w,h) with origin bottom-left.
(0,51,32,16): cassette-tape neon sign on a dark board (red rounded outline, two orange reels).
(0,35,32,16): grey hi-fi panel with a blue display, an orange display and two cream light tubes.
Doubt about these two: the panel has no top outline of its own (row 51 is the sign's outline). Together they form a 32x32 block with the same 16-px top / 16-px front split as the counter modules beside it. So they may be ONE floor unit (a music/DJ counter with the reels on a dark top; footprint about x1,y0,w30,h16) rather than a wall sign above a wall panel. Re-slice (0,35,32,32) whole and judge by eye.
(32,35,32,32): counter module with a light top over a double-door front, handles at the center seam. The left door carries a cyan robot-face display with text. ada_console candidate; footprint about x1,y0,w30,h16.
(64,35,32,32): counter module with a framed front screen showing 'OK' and text. Terminal candidate; same footprint.
(32,0,32,35): double-door counter module on 3-px legs (x1-2 and x29-30); footprint about x1,y0,w30,h16.
(64,0,32,35): single-panel module with a leg on its right end only (x28-29). It is the right-hand extension of (32,0); same footprint.
Each pair (upper and lower) shares a continuous top outline, so each pair also works as one 64-px counter, and the 64-px monitor rig 20/21/22 fits across one. Each light top is 30x13 and fits sink 16/17. In the sheet, sinks 16/17 sit directly above the upper pair, x-aligned with its light tops.

entries.label: Wide window frame, empty (cyan HUD trim)
entries.notes: 78x25 frame only. The interior is fully transparent, so the wall or a backdrop shows through. Use it over a backdrop or as an empty/off wall display. Cyan-trim version of 8 (orange) and 18 (pink), which are pixel-identical apart from the trim color. 27 is this same frame filled with a night-city view. Front-facing; hangs on the back wall.

entries.label: Panoramic window with night city skyline (cyan HUD trim)
entries.zoneUse: any room on an exterior wall: lounge, office, apartment, lobby
entries.notes: Frame 26 filled with a purple night skyline (lit windows, pink/yellow neon). Cyan HUD marks are drawn over the view, so it can also read as a big wall display. Cyan version of 9 (orange trim) and 19 (pink trim), same art. Front-facing, back wall.

entries.label: Computer keyboard
entries.zoneUse: office, control room, security, lab (on desks)
entries.notes: 14x7, pixel-identical to 37. In the sheet it sits centered under blue monitor 21 as part of the blue rig 20/21/22 + mouse 29, at offset (+9,-8) px from 21's bottom-left. Place on a desk top such as 35.

entries.label: Computer mouse
entries.zoneUse: office, control room, security, lab (on desks)
entries.notes: 4x5 px, pixel-identical to 38. Sits right of keyboard 28 in the blue rig, at offset (+27,-7) px from monitor 21's bottom-left. Identified as a mouse from context; could also pass as a tiny gadget or drive.

entries.label: Angled wing monitor, left (orange)
entries.zoneUse: office, control room, security, AI/ADA station
entries.notes: Left wing of the orange wrap-around triple-monitor rig (30|31|32 + keyboard 37 + mouse 38). The screen angles toward the viewer: the outer (left) edge column spans rows 0-16 and the inner (right) edge column spans rows 11-27. The top row 27 lines up with the top of monitor 31. No stand (floating or arm-mounted). Exact horizontal mirror of 32 (0 px differ). Blue version is 20, a pure palette swap (#ff5a00 to #14a0cd, #ffd461 to #82ffe1). Offset (-16,-8) px from 31's bottom-left. This pack draws side walls as thin vertical strips (see slices 0 and 39), so it does not hang flat on a side wall. Place it on the desk beside 31, or standalone as a floating holo-panel.

entries.label: Desktop monitor on stand (orange screen)
entries.notes: Center piece of the orange triple-monitor rig. The stand base is at rows 0-2, x=13-18 (row 2 narrows to x=14-17). Assembly per the sheet layout, offsets from 31's bottom-left in px: wing 30 (-16,-8), wing 32 (+34,-8), keyboard 37 (+9,-8), mouse 38 (+27,-7). The full rig is 64x28 px (4 tiles wide, under 2 tiles tall). The wings and keyboard share the bottom row; the wings and 31 share the top row. With the keyboard bottom on the front edge of desk 35's top (desk row 16), the stand lands on the top's back edge (desk row 24) and the rig top reaches desk row 43. The 58 px desk lets the wings overhang about 3 px per side. The full rig suits the ADA/AI-assistant station. 31+37+38 alone on a desk also works as an investigation terminal. Blue version: 21 (with 20/22/28/29), a pure palette swap.

entries.label: Angled wing monitor, right (orange)
entries.zoneUse: office, control room, security, AI/ADA station
entries.notes: Right wing of the orange triple-monitor rig. Exact horizontal mirror of 30 (0 px differ). The outer (right) edge column is nearer/lower (rows 0-16); the inner (left) edge column spans rows 11-27. Blue version is 22. Offset (+34,-8) px from monitor 31's bottom-left. No stand; place on the desk beside 31.

entries.label: Lounge chair, red (side view, facing right)
entries.notes: White shell chair. The backrest is on the left and rises to y=29. The red seat cushion is seen from above at x7-19, y7-18, with the near-side face of the seat at rows 0-5 and a far rim at rows 19-21. The bottom-left corner is rounded (row 0 spans x5-19). The footprint covers the seat depth; the backrest and far rim draw over a player standing behind. Faces right. 40 is its horizontal mirror facing left (646/660 px identical). Blue twin: 34.

entries.label: Lounge chair, blue (side view, facing right)
entries.notes: Blue twin of 33, 1 px wider (23 px; wider cushion), otherwise the same shape. 41 is its exact horizontal mirror (faces left). Footprint uses the same logic as 33: seat depth, base spans x=0-22, row 0 spans x5-20.

entries.label: Long desk / counter with cabinets
entries.zoneUse: office, reception, lab, security, control room
entries.notes: Front-facing. The front face is rows 0-15 (16 px, about 1 tile tall). The top surface is rows 16-24, exactly 9 px deep: outline #55647d on rows 16 and 24, light top on rows 17-22, white back highlight on row 23. Footprint h=9 matches that depth. Row 0 is transparent at x=0 and x=57 (rounded corners). The front has a left cabinet door with a red-framed cyan status badge (x~1-14), a middle double drawer split at row 8 (x~16-41) and a right cabinet door (x~43-56). A natural base for monitor rig 30/31/32 + 37/38, which together make a 4-tile workstation. Open-door variants of the same desk: 42 (left badge door open), 49 (right door open), 55 (both doors open). In those, the open door hangs 5-6 px below the base, so the desk body sits 5-6 px higher in the slice.

entries.label: Neon-framed arcade screen / poster (space shooter)
entries.zoneUse: lounge, break room, arcade corner, bedroom
entries.notes: Flat, front-facing 26x30 panel. Cyan neon frame around a purple starfield with two alien fighters and a player rocket with green thrusters, in a Galaga style. No stand or cabinet body, so hang it on the back wall as a game screen or poster.

entries.label: Computer keyboard (duplicate of 28)
entries.zoneUse: office, control room, security, lab (on desks)
entries.notes: Pixel-identical to 28. In the sheet it belongs to the orange rig, centered under monitor 31 at offset (+9,-8) px from 31's bottom-left.

entries.label: Computer mouse (duplicate of 29)
entries.zoneUse: office, control room, security, lab (on desks)
entries.notes: 4x5 px, pixel-identical to 29. Part of the orange rig, right of keyboard 37, at offset (+27,-7) px from monitor 31's bottom-left.

entries.label: Cross-shaped room wall outline
entries.notes: 114x120 plus-shaped wall ring, not furniture. Wall tops are #384753, 7 px thick, with a 1 px trim and a 1 px dark inner outline. The interior is transparent, to be filled with floor. The interior arms are 2 tiles wide: the vertical arm is x 41-72 by y 14-109 and the horizontal arm is x 9-104 by y 46-77. The south-facing outer wall faces are dark 7 px bands at y 0-6 (bottom arm) and y 32-38 (side arms). The north inner walls show a 3 px lighter face. Use it as a room-shape reference or slice it into wall pieces. Collision should come from the wall tilemap, not from this sprite.

entries.label: Red armchair, side view facing left
entries.notes: Part of a 4-direction armchair set: 23 front, 33 side facing right, 40 side facing left, 46 back. Blue twin is 41. 33 is only a near-mirror of 40, not an exact one: flipX(33) differs from 40 in 14 px (backrest inner slope at x 10-13, y 20-25, and the cushion's lower-right edge at x 13, y 6-9). flipX on 40 therefore approximates 33 but is not pixel-identical, unlike 41, which is an exact mirror of 34. The backrest sits on the right edge (x 14-21) and rises to y=29. The red seat cushion is at x 2-14, y 7-18. The seat area spans y 6-21 including its outlines, and its interior y 7-20 is 14 px, so the depth is about 14-16 px. The footprint covers the full base width (x 0-21).

entries.label: Blue armchair, side view facing left
entries.notes: Blue twin of 40 and mirror of 34. Blue set: 24 front, 34 facing right, 41 facing left, 47 back. The backrest is on the right edge (x 15-22) and rises to y=29. The blue cushion is at x 3-15, y 7-18. Same depth logic as 40.

entries.label: Long storage cabinet, left display door open
entries.notes: Cabinet set: 35 all closed, 42 left door open, 49 right door open, 55 both doors open. The body base is at y=5. Rows 0-4 hold only the swung-open left door (x 4-10), which is thin and left out of the footprint. When swapping with the closed version 35 (base at y=0), offset the pivot by 5 px. The left door carries a red-framed keypad/status screen. The light-blue top is 9 px deep (y 21-29) and the front face is 16 px. Faces down. The open variants work well as a 'searched' evidence cabinet.

entries.label: Two-door smart fridge, closed
entries.notes: Set: 43 closed, 44 upper door open, 45 lower door open. Taller than the player (front face y 0-29). The top surface is y 30-45, about 15-16 px deep. The upper door has a digital readout and the lower door a small cyan control screen; both handles are on the left. Faces down. Could also stand in for a food/drink vending unit.

entries.label: Two-door smart fridge, upper door open
entries.notes: Upper-door-open variant of 43, with the same size and base at y=0, so it swaps in place. Red and blue drink/food packs show on the shelf at y 20-25. The open door is drawn as a white edge strip at x 1-4.

entries.label: Two-door smart fridge, lower door open
entries.notes: Lower-door-open variant of 43. The sprite is 28x48 because the swung-open door (x 0-4) hangs 2 px below the body to y=0; it is excluded from the footprint. The body base is at y=2, so offset the pivot by 2 px when swapping with 43/44. Two shelves are visible: food packs at y 12-16, and purple bottles plus orange food at y 5-9. The top surface is y 32-47.

entries.label: Red armchair, back view
entries.notes: Back of red armchair 23 (same 25 px width): the seat faces up, away from the viewer, and has a red logo plate on the backrest. Set: 23/33/40/46; blue twin is 47. No seat surface is visible, so the depth (about 12) is estimated from the other views. The armrests show at the outer edges, x 0-1 and x 23-24.

entries.label: Blue armchair, back view
entries.notes: Back of blue armchair 24 (same 26 px width): faces up, away from the viewer, with a blue logo plate. Set: 24/34/41/47; red twin is 46. Depth is estimated the same way as 46.

entries.label: Large white L-shaped desk
entries.notes: Blank light slab on a dark pedestal (x 5-53, front face y 0-10). On the left the slab runs from a black front outline at y=11 to the back outline at y=28: 1 px front edge band at y=12, top fill y 13-26, back highlight y=27. That makes it a full 16 px tile deep, so the footprint uses the 16 px cap. The slab overhangs the pedestal by 5 px on each side (x 0-4 and x 54-58), and the footprint uses the full slab width so the player cannot stand under the overhang. The right section juts 5 px toward the viewer (its front outline is at y=6 vs y=11 on the left). A small blue-lit unit sits under it (x 44-51, y 3-5). That wing overhangs the floor slightly south of the pedestal base, so a player just below y=0 at x 42-58 may overlap it; extend the collider there only if it shows. Nothing sits on the top: add monitor 21/31 and keyboard 28/37 to make a workstation. Good base for an ADA or reception station once dressed. Similar style to the smaller slab 6.

entries.label: Long storage cabinet with display, right door open
entries.notes: Cabinet set: 35/42/49/55. The left door is closed and shows a red-framed keypad/status screen (mint glyphs). The right door (x 43-56) is swung open and hangs below the base to y=0 at x 47-53; it is left out of the footprint. The base is at y=5. The top is 9 px deep (y 22-30), and this sprite is 1 px taller than 42. Offset the pivot by 5 px against the closed version 35.

entries.label: Slim wall lamp with orange light
entries.notes: 10x28 capsule light fixture. It has a glowing orange/yellow lens at the top, in the same #ffd461/#ff9c28 palette as neon bars 51-53, plus two small vent slits. The bottom is a 4 px stem that tapers to a point at y=0, with no base plate. The symmetric front-on drawing reads as a wall sconce or beacon. Doubt: it could also be a slim standing light post. If it is placed on the floor, give it a small collider of about x=3, y=0, w=4, h=3.

entries.label: Orange neon light tube
entries.notes: 24x5 glowing orange bar with a yellow highlight row and rounded corners. Pixel-identical to 53. 52 is a brighter frame 1 px taller, so 51-52-53 are probably a glow/flicker animation loop. Horizontal neon strip for walls; it could also work as a floor or ceiling light strip. It has no emitter end caps, unlike the red laser beam 54.

entries.label: Orange neon light bar (thick)
entries.notes: 24x6 glowing orange tube with rounded ends: FF5A00 outline, 2 yellow FFD461 highlight rows (y3-4) over 2 orange FF9C28 rows (y1-2). This is the thick bar in the set; 51 and 53 are the thin ones and are pixel-identical to each other (1 highlight row). On the sheet 51/52/53 are stacked thin/thick/thin with 1 px gaps (24x18 total), so they can be combined into one three-bar neon sign, or swapped as a glow pulse (51/53 dim, 52 bright). Uses the same orange palette as door 57 and the orange screens. No bracket is drawn. It could also be laid flat as a floor neon strip (floor_detail). Doubt: could be a plain orange shelf board, but the glow colors suggest neon.

entries.label: Orange neon light bar (thin)
entries.notes: 24x5: FF5A00 outline, 1 yellow highlight row (y3) over 2 orange rows (y1-2). Pixel-identical to 51 and the thinner version of 52. It is the bottom bar of the 51/52/53 stack on the sheet. Wall accent lighting, not solid.

entries.label: Red neon tube light with end clamps
entries.notes: 58x6: red tube spanning x=2-55 (dark-red 740801 edge rows, pink FF9392 highlight row y3, C6100F core y2), held by 3x6 dark clamps at x=0-2 and x=55-57. Same 58 px width as desks 35/42/49/55, so it can go above a desk or along a counter. On the sheet it sits directly under hover bench 48 and may be meant as that bench's red under-glow. It could also pass for a red laser-barrier beam, but it has no emitter posts, so treat it as non-solid decor.

entries.label: Cabinet desk, both doors open
entries.notes: Front-facing 58x30 cabinet desk: light top y21-29 (white back-edge highlight at y28) and dark front panel y5-20. The body's bottom outline (y5, x1-56) is the real floor line. Variants: 35 (all closed, 58x25, same 25 px body), 42 (left red-framed display door open), 49 (right cabinet door open). Here BOTH doors swing toward the viewer and their tips hang below the body to y=0 at x=4-10 and x=47-53 (rows 0-4 are otherwise transparent), so the footprint starts at y=5. Thin extra colliders for the door tips are optional. Swap alignment: 42, 49 and 55 all have the body base at y=5, but closed 35 has it at y=0. To swap 35 for an open variant in place, shift the open sprite down 5 px (align the footprint bottoms) so the desk does not jump up. Monitors 20-22, keyboard 28 or plates can sit on top.

entries.label: Bed pillow
entries.notes: 21x14 puffy pale-blue/white pillow seen from above, with tufted corners and a white highlight blob. Overlay for bed 68 (41 px wide): center it at the head end, around x=10-30, y=33-46 of the bed. Bed 68's mattress is only y9-47 (39 px), above a 9 px control panel at y0-8. Blanket 69 (blue) or 70 (orange) is 35 px tall, so blanket plus pillow is 49 px. The pillow therefore overlaps the top of the blanket by roughly 5-10 px and must be drawn over it. Here 'desk' placement means 'on top of furniture'. It could also work as a walkable floor cushion in a lounge.

entries.label: Sliding door, closed
entries.zoneUse: any (room entrance on a back/north wall)
entries.notes: 42x46 front-facing sci-fi door in a gray frame: orange leaf x=9-32 (24 px = 1.5 tiles) with a white circuit line and logo, frame posts x=0-8 and x=33-41, keypad on the right post (x=35-39, y=14-22). Closed state of 58. The base row y=0 spans the full width. The footprint is a thin blocker along the wall line, since the wall tiles behind it provide the depth. When swapping to 58, free x=9-32 and keep the posts blocked.

entries.label: Sliding door, open
entries.zoneUse: any (room entrance on a back/north wall)
entries.notes: Open state of 57: the orange leaf has slid into the left pocket (a 5 px sliver at x=9-13), leaving a dark walkable opening at x=14-32, y=0-39. The doorway is passable, but the frame posts (x=0-8 and x=33-41) still need blocking from the wall collider, because a single-rect footprint cannot describe two posts. Same keypad as 57.

entries.label: Sci-fi supply chest, closed
entries.notes: 28x28 crate in 3/4 view: blue lid with two gray straps and orange/red side handles (top surface y12-25; strap latches reach y27), dark front y0-11 with cyan/blue side lights and a yellow/orange center lock. Body x=0-27, bottom row x=2-25. Closed variant of 60, which has the same front and base.

entries.label: Sci-fi supply chest, open
entries.notes: Open variant of 59: same front y0-11, open box interior y12-20 (lit front rim, shadowed back) and the lid raised behind it at y21-29. The box reads about 9 px deep, hence h=9. If you swap 59 and 60 at runtime, just keep 59's collider (h=14).

entries.label: Table with lit top, blue trim
entries.notes: 46x36: pale C8E1EB top with an inset blue (14A0CD) border and 'TIP' logo, beveled gray frame, dark front edge at y6, and two chunky front legs at x=0-11 and x=34-45 (y0-5). The visible top is about 29 px deep (y7-35), so h is capped at 16. Pairs with red 62. Its palette matches blue chairs 24/34/41 and pod 47, which suggests a dining or meeting set; plates 63-65 and mug 66 can sit on top. Doubt: it can also be read as a big display/TV on two feet. In that case the footprint would be just the feet (h about 6), and it would suit an ADA screen.

entries.label: Table with lit top, red trim
entries.notes: Red variant of 61: D72D2D border and pink FFE0E0 top, with the same frame, legs and 'TIP' logo. It matches red chairs 23/33/40 and pod 46. Same footprint and same TV-reading doubt as 61 (as a TV, the footprint would be just the feet, h about 6).

entries.label: Pizza on plate
entries.zoneUse: break room, kitchen, lounge, office desk
entries.notes: 16x8 whole pepperoni pizza (brown crust, yellow cheese, red slices) on a white plate with a dark 494949 rim. Same plate shape as 64 and 65. Place it on tables 61/62 or on desk tops.

entries.label: Plate with leftovers
entries.zoneUse: break room, kitchen, lounge, office desk
entries.notes: 16x8 white plate with leftover crumbs. The center is bare white and the light-gray inner ring shows, as on empty plate 65. There are scattered cream/tan bits, a 2 px green herb and one red bit (F23117, the same red as the pepperoni on 63). It could also read as a light plate of rice with a garnish. Same plate as 63 (pizza) and 65 (empty), and the sheet row 63-64-65 reads as full, eaten, clean. Place it on tables or desks.

entries.label: Empty white plate
entries.zoneUse: kitchen / cafeteria / lounge / break room (on tables or counters)
entries.notes: Empty variant of plates 63 (pizza) and 64 (food on plate). All three are 16x8 and sit in the same sheet row, so they swap in place. Oval seen in 3/4 view: #494949 outline, white face, faint #E5DEDE inner-rim shading at rows 2-3. Decoration only, no collider.

entries.label: White coffee mug
entries.zoneUse: office / lounge / kitchen (on desks or tables)
entries.notes: 11x10 grey-white mug with the handle on the RIGHT side (x=7-10, rows 3-6). Grey #898989 interior at rows 5-7 reads as empty. Goes with red cup 67 and plates 63-65 as desk clutter.

entries.label: Red drink cup
entries.notes: 8x9 pink-red cup with no handle (#E88787 body, #721922 outline, white glints). Red drink or dark interior at rows 5-6. Could also pass as a small jar. Companion to mug 66. Sits lower on the sheet than 63-66 but belongs to the same food/drink group.

entries.label: Bed base (white mattress, footboard control panel)
entries.zoneUse: bedroom / crew quarters / rest area / med bay
entries.notes: Bare bed. Cream mattress top (y=9-46, 38 px deep; 40 px including its #5F5547 outline at y=8 and y=47) above an 8 px footboard panel (y=0-7, #212B35 outline) with red and cyan indicator capsules that suit either blanket color. For a made bed, overlay blanket 69 (blue) or 70 (orange) at 68-local offset (-3,+9). Make 68 the root, put a SortingGroup on it and add the blanket as a child with order +1 inside the group. Props and the player share sortingOrder 2 under CustomAxis y-sort (GameWorldBuilder.cs), so a plain sortingOrder bump on the blanket would draw it over a player standing in front of the bed. Optionally hang rail 71/72 on the wall just above at (-3,+48). Composite check: C:\Users\johan\AppData\Local\Temp\claude_catalog_ctx\composites2.png. Faces the camera: foot at the bottom, head at the top. Place the head against the back wall or add a blocker. The real mattress depth (38-40 px) is more than the 16 px footprint cap, so otherwise the player can walk into the upper bed from the side and be hidden behind it. Bottom rows 0-1 have rounded corners (x=2-38 and x=1-39); full width (x=0-40) from row 2. Sheet-wide: every sprite in the .meta uses alignment 0 (Center pivot, PPU 16), so y-sorting needs a bottom pivot or sort point.

entries.label: Blue blanket (bed cover overlay)
entries.notes: Duvet overlay for bed 68 at 68-local offset (-3,+9). Make it a child of 68 under a SortingGroup on 68, with order +1 inside the group. Do not just raise its sortingOrder: props and the player share sortingOrder 2 under CustomAxis y-sort, so it would draw over a player standing in front of the bed. Covers the mattress. The hem (rows 1-6) flares 2-3 px past both bed sides; the middle rows (10-31, x=2-43) overhang only 1 px on the left and are flush on the right. Corner tips reach bed y=9, just above the frame line and footboard. A 3 px cream strip stays at the head, and a 2-3 px cream band shows under the middle of the hem (composite checked). No collider; 68 provides it. Blue twin of 70: identical alpha mask, near-exact palette swap (4 fold-shading pixels differ, at (13,7), (13,14), (14,26), (14,28)). Matches blue rail 71. Creases and two bumps at the top (row 34, x=6-19 and x=32-39) suggest pillows under the cover. Standalone use is unlikely. If ever used alone, make it solid with a footprint of about (1,2,45,12), since rows 0-1 are only corner tips and the opaque width at rows 3-6 is x=1-45.

entries.label: Orange blanket (bed cover overlay)
entries.notes: Orange/red twin of 69: identical alpha mask, near-exact palette swap (#186088->#883000, #14A0CD->#FF5A00, #1A79AE->#C64600, #104461->#740801; 4 fold-shading pixels differ, at (13,7), (13,14), (14,26), (14,28)). Duvet overlay for bed 68 at 68-local offset (-3,+9), as a child of 68 under a SortingGroup with order +1 inside the group. A plain sortingOrder bump would draw it over a player standing in front of the bed, because props and the player share sortingOrder 2. No collider; 68 provides it. Matches orange rail 72. If ever used standalone, make it solid with a footprint of about (1,2,45,12); rows 0-1 are only corner tips.

entries.label: Wall light rail with two blue lamps
entries.zoneUse: bedroom (headboard light above bed 68) / lounge / corridor accent lighting
entries.notes: Front view of a horizontal rod (rows 2-5). Matching wall brackets at both ends (x=0-1 and x=44-45, ticks at rows 1 and 6). Two glowing lamp boxes at x=6-12 and x=33-39 with a triangle-over-bar icon. Icon centers are about (9,4) and (36,4), good spots for Light2D. Blue twin of 72 (identical alpha mask). Same 46 px width as blankets 69/70. Hung on the wall right above bed 68 (68-local offset -3,+48), it reads as a headboard reading-lamp rail. The brackets look like wall mounts, not floor posts, so it is not a floor barrier.

entries.label: Wall light rail with two orange lamps
entries.zoneUse: bedroom (headboard light above bed 68) / lounge / corridor accent lighting
entries.notes: Orange twin of 71 (identical alpha mask): orange lamp boxes with yellow icons and dark-red outlines. Lamp icon centers are about (9,4) and (36,4). Goes with orange blanket 70 above bed 68 at 68-local offset (-3,+48). Wall decoration, no collider.
